verdict.rationale: LlamaParse's own docs describe it as layout-aware OCR that turns complex layouts into clean, LLM-ready markdown. One hands-on user also praised its output on a complex-layout document. Neither source explicitly documents preserving headings, section hierarchy or reading order, and markdown output only implies structure. missing for 10: explicit documentation of heading/section hierarchy preservation, documented reading-order handling for multi-column layouts, independent corroboration of structural fidelity.

support.subject: As an ML engineer, parsed output preserves document hierarchy — headings, sections, reading order — so downstream LLMs see structure, not soup

citations.quote: layout-aware OCR that turns PDFs, scans, tables, and charts into clean markdown, text, or JSON
Turn even the most complex layouts, tables, charts, handwriting, checkboxes, and images into clean markdown
it reads tables, charts, scanned pages, and 130+ file types with layout-aware accuracy that generic OCR and PDF-to-text tools can’t match
